Best CRM for Freelancers & Solo Owners

A freelancer does not need the same CRM as a sales team. The best CRM for a solo business is the one that tracks clients and follow-ups in minutes, not the one with the most features. Here are the tools that fit a one-person operation — and which to avoid.

By The GridDojo Team Published August 27, 2026 4 min read

Most "best CRM" advice is written for sales teams, and it steers solo workers toward tools far heavier than they need. As a freelancer, consultant, or solo owner, you are not managing a team's pipeline — you are keeping track of clients, proposals, and the follow-ups that are easy to forget when you are also doing the actual work. The best CRM for you is the one that does that in minutes and then gets out of the way.

What a solo business actually needs

  • Simplicity. You will set it up and maintain it alone, so it has to be genuinely quick to use.
  • Low or no cost. Per-user pricing is not the issue; you are one user, so a free or cheap plan is plenty.
  • Contacts and follow-ups. A clear place for every client and a reminder so nothing is dropped.
  • A light pipeline. Enough to see inquiries, proposals sent, and work won — not a 12-stage sales funnel.
  • Fits where you work. If you live in Gmail or a specific tool, a CRM that sits there beats one you have to open separately.

The best CRMs for freelancers and solo owners

These tools are chosen for simplicity and low cost rather than depth. Plans and limits change often, so confirm the current details on each vendor's pricing page before you commit.

Bigin and Capsule — simple pipelines, low cost

Bigin, Zoho's lightweight CRM, is built for exactly this: a solo owner or micro-team who wants a clean pipeline without the weight of a full sales platform, at a low price with a usable free tier. Capsule is similarly minimal and contact-first, with a free tier for very small use. Both take minutes to learn.

Best for: solo owners who want a real but simple pipeline. Skip them if: you need heavy automation or marketing tools.

Streak — a CRM inside Gmail

If your client work happens over email, Streak adds a CRM directly inside Gmail, so you track inquiries, proposals, and follow-ups without leaving your inbox. For freelancers who manage relationships mostly by email, that lack of context-switching is the whole appeal, and there is a free plan for solo use.

Best for: freelancers who live in Gmail. Skip it if: you do not use Gmail or want a CRM independent of your email.

HubSpot Free and Less Annoying CRM — professional but easy

HubSpot's free CRM gives a solo business a polished, professional setup at no cost, with plenty of room to grow if you later add help. Less Annoying CRM takes the opposite route — one simple plan at a flat price, designed specifically for small and solo operations that want zero complexity.

Best for: a free professional start (HubSpot) or flat-price simplicity (Less Annoying CRM). Skip them if: HubSpot's breadth feels like too much, or you would rather not pay a flat monthly fee as a solo user.

Do you even need a CRM yet?

If you are tracking only a few clients, a spreadsheet may still be enough — there is no prize for adopting software early. Our guide to CRM vs spreadsheet covers exactly where that line is. And if you decide a full CRM is overkill, an AI assistant for small business tasks can help with the client emails and proposals a CRM would otherwise organise.

Frequently asked questions

What is the best CRM for a freelancer?

For most freelancers, a simple, low-cost tool like Bigin, Capsule, or Less Annoying CRM fits best, while Streak suits those who work mainly in Gmail and HubSpot's free tier offers a professional start. The right pick depends on where you work and how simple you want it.

Do solo business owners really need a CRM?

Only once tracking clients and follow-ups in your head or a spreadsheet starts causing missed opportunities. If you are dropping follow-ups or losing track of proposals, a lightweight CRM helps; if not, a simple spreadsheet may still be enough.

Is there a free CRM good enough for a solo business?

Yes. HubSpot's free CRM, Bigin's and Capsule's free tiers, and Streak's free plan are all genuinely usable for one person. Free limits on contacts and features rarely bite for a solo operation until you grow.
